description: European company search: company lookup by name across official European company registers, in one unified schema. Local copies, all searched when pays is absent: Belgium, Croatia, Cyprus, Estonia, Ireland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, Romania, Sweden, Spain (BORME base, hoja key); live, only with pays set: Czechia, Finland, Slovakia, Switzerland; Poland through GLEIF (no name search at the register); Denmark and the United Kingdom live, only with pays set; plus worldwide GLEIF (LEI) coverage. Each match carries a score_confiance (0-1 match confidence). nombre_resultats counts every servable result the registers returned (tronque: true beyond the 10 served, note_troncature when it is a lower bound). Czechia, Estonia, Norway, Latvia and Slovakia serve legal persons only: a sole trader (in Estonia, a sole proprietorship, FIE; in Norway, a sole proprietorship, ENK, a registered individual or an estate; in Latvia, an individual merchant, IK, or an individual, family, farm or fishery enterprise; in Slovakia, any entity of the trade register, and one of the commercial register) or a form not recognised as a legal person is left out; Croatia too (a trgovac pojedinac, t.p., or an undecided form); in Denmark, a sole proprietorship (ENK), a personally owned small business (PMV), an estate (DØD) or an undecided CVR form; in Lithuania, an individual enterprise (individuali įmonė, IĮ), its branch (individualios įmonės filialas) or representative office (individualios įmonės atstovybė), or an undecided form; in Finland, Ireland and the United Kingdom, a form outside the register's published nomenclature; in Belgium, an entity without legal form or of a form off the whitelist, and in Spain, the hoja of a sole trader (a BORME empresario individual act), are left out; in Switzerland, a sole proprietorship (Einzelunternehmen, whose name carries the owner's name), a branch (the search does not know its head office) or an undecided legal form is left out; in every country, a GLEIF LEI of a natural person (sole proprietor category or natural-person legal form) or of an ambiguous legal form is left out too, its legal form written as free text included; a GLEIF LEI (general or branch) of a country with a local copy is served only when that copy knows and serves its number, a branch under the country of its legal address; all are counted by reason in ecartes, never named. A search Zefix or ARES refuses as too broad returns requete_trop_large, not charged: refine the name; a register or database outage returns 503 with the code naming it (amont_indisponible, base_indisponible), never charged. Spanish matches return the hoja registral to use with get_spanish_company_acts. Paid via x402 ($0.003 in USDC or EURC).

api_key.description: Optional Sirenic API key (srn_live_…) to pay with prepaid credits instead of x402 — no wallet needed. Get one at https://api.sirenic.eu/compte. Ignored when x_payment is provided (the signed payment wins). On insufficient balance the tool returns a credits error, not an x402 quote.

pays.description: Optional ISO-3166 alpha-2 country filter, e.g. NO, EE, LV

q.description: Company name (2 characters minimum once cleaned up, 3 with pays=CH). Unsupported characters are stripped, not rejected.

x_payment.description: Optional signed x402 PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header value. Omit to receive the payment quote.

name: search_european_companies

hint.description: How to settle the quote, present when payment_required is true.

payment_required.description: True when this response is an x402 payment quote instead of data: settle one of the quote's `accepts` options and call the tool again with `x_payment`.

quote.description: The signable x402 payment requirements when payment_required is true: {x402Version, accepts[]} where each entry carries scheme, network, amount, asset and payTo (USDC and EURC options at the same numeric amount). Sign one entry and call again with `x_payment`.

resultat.description: The endpoint's JSON response when payment_required is false. Paid responses carry `source`, `disclaimer` and an Ed25519 signature, and every paid JSON response carries a `provenance` array (all tools since 2026-09-06) — one entry per block served, with the official register, licence, version, `as_of` date and `precision_as_of` (what that date means), plus the common per-block envelope: `etat` in a closed list (servi, absence_mesuree, absence_non_conclusive, partiel, perime, indisponible, sans_objet), `motif` when unavailable, `age_jours` (only for publication or ingestion dates), `couverture` (complete / partielle / non_mesurable with its measure) and `confiance` in bands (faible / moyenne / forte, only where a measure grounds it, never averaged across blocks). Read the states before the numbers: an absence_non_conclusive, indisponible or partiel block is never « nothing to report » — only absence_mesuree asserts an absence. Register codes: GET /v1/provenance/registres ; states, closed lists and reading rules: GET /v1/lecture (both free). The PDF tools carry no JSON envelope (the PDF report prints it).

title: Search European companies by name
